cues.text: IN THE MOUNTAINS ABOVE BERGEN, NORWAY, THERE IS A VALLEY CALLED ISDALEN —
THE ICE VALLEY. IN LATE NOVEMBER 1970, IT GAVE UP ONE OF THE STRANGEST CASES IN EUROPEAN CRIMINAL HISTORY.
A WOMAN WAS FOUND DEAD ON THE VALLEY FLOOR. SHE HAD BURNED.
AND SOMEONE HAD CAREFULLY REMOVED EVERY TRACE OF WHO SHE WAS —
FROM HER CLOTHES, HER BELONGINGS, AND HER LUGGAGE.
SHE CARRIED NO NAME. INSTEAD SHE LEFT THE OPPOSITE OF A CONFESSION:
EIGHT FALSE IDENTITIES, A CODED NOTEBOOK, AND A SET OF CLUES SO STRANGE THAT INVESTIGATORS
HAVE ARGUED ABOUT THEM FOR MORE THAN FIFTY YEARS.
THIS IS THE FILE OF THE ISDAL WOMAN. NOT A STORY ABOUT WHO KILLED HER.
A STORY ABOUT A WOMAN WHO ERASED HERSELF — AND THE QUESTIONS THAT ERASURE LEFT BEHIND.
BERGEN POLICE OPENED THE CASE UNDER A DRY BUREAUCRATIC LABEL:
NUMBER 134, OF 1970. HALF A CENTURY LATER, THE FILE IS STILL OPEN.
THE QUESTION AT THE CENTRE OF IT HAS NEVER CHANGED.
WHO CHECKED INTO NORWAY'S HOTELS UNDER EIGHT DIFFERENT NAMES —
AND WHY DID SHE NEED ALL OF THEM?
IT WAS A SUNDAY MORNING, THE TWENTY-NINTH OF NOVEMBER 1970.
A FATHER AND HIS TWO YOUNG DAUGHTERS WERE HIKING THE FOOTHILLS BELOW THE NORTH FACE OF ULRIKEN,
ONE OF BERGEN'S SEVEN MOUNTAINS.
THE VALLEY BETWEEN THE SLOPES HAD A SECOND NAME —
DEATH VALLEY — EARNED BY MEDIEVAL HISTORY AND BY ACCIDENTS ON ITS TREACHEROUS SCREE.
THAT MORNING IT LIVED UP TO NEITHER. IT SIMPLY HELD SOMETHING NO ONE EXPECTED.
AMONG THE ROCKS, THE FAMILY FOUND THE BODY OF A WOMAN.
SHE WAS LYING ON HER BACK. THERE WAS EVIDENCE OF A SMALL FIRE NEARBY.
THE FRONT OF HER BODY AND HER CLOTHING HAD BEEN BURNED; HER FACE COULD NOT BE RECOGNISED.
THE DAUGHTERS WERE WALKED HOME. THE POLICE WERE CALLED.
WITHIN HOURS, THE VALLEY FLOOR HAD BECOME A SCENE OF EVIDENCE.
AROUND HER LAY A STRANGE INVENTORY. AN EMPTY BOTTLE OF ST.
HALLVARD LIQUEUR. TWO PLASTIC WATER BOTTLES. A PLASTIC PASSPORT HOLDER — EMPTY.
RUBBER BOOTS. A WOOLLEN JUMPER. A SCARF. NYLON STOCKINGS.
AN UMBRELLA. A PURSE, A MATCHBOX, A WATCH, TWO EARRINGS, AND A RING.
BENEATH HER BODY, A FUR HAT WOULD LATER TEST POSITIVE FOR PETROL.
AROUND IT, THE TRACES OF BURNED PAPER.
AND ONE DETAIL ABOVE ALL: ON NEARLY EVERY ITEM, THE LABELS, MARKS AND NAME-TAGS HAD BEEN REMOVED
OR RUBBED AWAY. NOT LOST. REMOVED.
AT THE GADES INSTITUTE IN BERGEN, THE POST-MORTEM BUILT A MEDICAL TIMELINE.
THE WOMAN HAD DIED FROM A COMBINATION OF SLEEPING TABLETS AND CARBON MONOXIDE.
HER BLOOD HELD THE EQUIVALENT OF FIFTY TO SEVENTY FENEMAL TABLETS —
A BARBITURATE THAT BRINGS SLEEP, THEN STOPS THE LUNGS.
TWELVE MORE PILLS WERE FOUND BESIDE THE BODY.
SOOT IN HER AIRWAYS SHOWED SHE WAS STILL ALIVE AS THE FIRE REACHED HER.
A BRUISE ON HER NECK COULD HAVE COME FROM A FALL —
OR FROM A BLOW. THE REPORT COULD NOT SAY WHICH.
HER DENTAL WORK WAS SO DISTINCTIVE THAT INVESTIGATORS REMOVED HER TEETH AND JAW FOR EXAMINATION.
THAT DECISION WOULD MATTER, DECADES LATER.
THREE DAYS AFTER THE DISCOVERY, TWO SUITCASES WERE LOCATED AT BERGEN RAILWAY STATION, LEFT
BEHIND AS IF THEIR OWNER HAD SIMPLY STEPPED AWAY.
INSIDE: CLOTHING, SHOES, WIGS, MAKE-UP, ECZEMA CREAM, MAPS AND TIMETABLES.
COINS FROM BELGIUM, BRITAIN AND SWITZERLAND. A PAIR OF ORDINARY GLASSES —
AND SUNGLASSES WHOSE PARTIAL FINGERPRINTS MATCHED THE DEAD WOMAN.
SEWN INTO THE LINING OF ONE SUITCASE, POLICE FOUND FIVE HUNDRED DEUTSCHE MARKS —
REAL MONEY IN 1970, LEFT DELIBERATELY OR FORGOTTEN.
AND AGAIN, THE SAME SIGNATURE. EVERY IDENTIFICATION MARK ON EVERY ITEM —
INSIDE AND OUT — HAD BEEN CUT AWAY OR FILED OFF.
THE TRAIL LED BACK THROUGH BERGEN'S HOTELS TO THE HOTEL HORDAHEIMEN.
THE WOMAN HAD STAYED THERE IN MID-NOVEMBER 1970, IN ROOM 407.
STAFF REMEMBERED A WOMAN ABOUT FIVE FEET FOUR, DARK BROWN HAIR, SMALL BROWN EYES, GOOD-LOOKING.
SHE KEPT TO HER ROOM. SHE SEEMED, ONE ACCOUNT SAYS, TO BE ON GUARD.
SHE TOLD PEOPLE SHE WAS A TRAVELLING SALESWOMAN —
SOMETIMES AN ANTIQUITIES DEALER. WITNESSES NOTED WIGS.
MORE THAN ONE PERSON REMEMBERED THE SMELL OF GARLIC.
ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF NOVEMBER SHE PAID HER BILL IN CASH, ASKED FOR A TAXI, AND CHECKED OUT.
SHE WAS LAST SEEN ALIVE THAT DAY. WHAT HAPPENED IN THE SIX DAYS AFTER THAT IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE.
HER HOTEL REGISTRATION FORMS READ LIKE A CAST OF CHARACTERS.
GENEVIEVE LANCIER OF LEUVEN. CLAUDIA TIELT OF BRUSSELS.
CLAUDIA NIELSEN. VERA JARLE. FENELLA LORCK. ELISABETH LEENHOWER OF OSTEND.
EIGHT OR MORE NAMES, ON HANDWRITTEN FORMS FILLED OUT IN FRENCH AND GERMAN.
OCCUPATIONS AND BIRTHDAYS CHANGED FROM FORM TO FORM.
ONE THING NEVER DID: SHE ALWAYS GAVE HER NATIONALITY AS BELGIAN.
LATER, INVESTIGATORS CHECKED THE ADDRESSES. ALMOST EVERY STREET NAME ON THE FORMS WAS FALSE
— SEVERAL, IT TURNED OUT, DID NOT EXIST AT ALL.
MANY OF THE NAMES WERE SAINTS' NAMES. WHETHER THAT WAS DEVOTION, HABIT, OR A PRIVATE JOKE,
NO ONE HAS EVER ESTABLISHED.
IN ONE SUITCASE, POLICE FOUND A SMALL NOTEPAD. ITS PAGES CARRIED ENTRIES IN CODE —
LETTERS AND FIGURES IN ROWS THAT LOOKED LIKE NONSENSE.
INVESTIGATORS CRACKED IT. THE CODE WAS SIMPLE: LETTER SUBSTITUTIONS THAT OPENED ONTO DATES
AND PLACE NAMES. IT WAS A TRAVEL LOG, WRITTEN IN A PRIVATE SHORTHAND.
WHAT THE NOTEBOOK ESTABLISHES IS A ROUTE. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH IS A REASON.
THE ENTRIES MAP WHERE SHE WENT — NOT WHO SHE MET, AND NOT WHY SHE TRAVELLED.
IT IS THE PATTERN OF A PERSON MANAGING HER OWN SECRECY.
ANALYSTS AGREE ON THAT MUCH. BEYOND IT, THE CODE KEEPS ITS SILENCE.
RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE CODE, THE RECEIPTS AND THE HOTEL FORMS, HER LAST MONTHS LOOK LIKE THIS:
OSLO. TRONDHEIM. STAVANGER. THEN BERGEN — TWICE —
AND AT LEAST ONE TRIP THROUGH PARIS.
IN STAVANGER, A SHOE SALESMAN REMEMBERED SELLING RUBBER BOOTS TO A WELL-DRESSED WOMAN.
IN BERGEN, A WITNESS OVERHEARD HER SPEAKING GERMAN WITH A MAN IN A HOTEL.
OTHERS RECALLED FLEMISH, OR CAREFUL, BROKEN ENGLISH.
SHE CHANGED HOTEL ROOMS AFTER CHECKING IN. SHE WATCHED THE STREET FROM WINDOWS, WITNESSES
SAID. EVERY HABIT POINTED THE SAME DIRECTION: THIS WAS A WOMAN PRACTISED AT NOT BEING FOUND.
THE INVESTIGATION RAN FOR MONTHS AND CONSUMED ENORMOUS POLICE RESOURCES.
INTERPOL CIRCULATED THE COMPOSITE SKETCHES ACROSS EUROPE.
NO MISSING-PERSON REPORT MATCHED HER. NO FAMILY EVER CAME FORWARD.
IN 1971, BERGEN POLICE CLOSED THE CASE WITH A VERDICT OF PROBABLE SUICIDE.
THE WOMAN WHO COULD NOT BE NAMED WAS BURIED ON THE FIFTH OF FEBRUARY 1971, IN A ZINC COFFIN,
IN BERGEN'S MOLLENDAL CEMETERY. SIXTEEN POLICE OFFICERS ATTENDED.
THE VERDICT SETTLED THE FILE. IT NEVER SETTLED THE ARGUMENT.
TAKE THE OFFICIAL VERDICT SERIOUSLY, BECAUSE THE EVIDENCE ALLOWS IT.
THE TOXICOLOGY SUPPORTS A SELF-ADMINISTERED OVERDOSE.
THE SCENE HELD NO WEAPON AND NO SIGN OF STRUGGLE.
THE ERASED IDENTITY FITS ONE READING: A PERSON PREPARING TO DISAPPEAR.
CUTTING LABELS, PAYING CASH, FALSE NAMES — THE LOGISTICS OF SOMEONE WHO DID NOT WANT TO BE
TRACED, IN LIFE OR IN DEATH.
BUT IT EXPLAINS THE METHOD, NOT THE PLANNING. WHY TRAVEL A THOUSAND KILOMETRES TO DIE IN A
VALLEY? WHY THE NOTEBOOK OF DATES AND PLACES NO ONE WAS EVER MEANT TO READ?
OTHER DETAILS PULL THE OTHER WAY. THE BRUISE ON THE NECK.
A POSITION AND A FIRE THAT A DEEPLY SEDATED PERSON MAY NOT HAVE MANAGED ALONE.
IN 1991, A TAXI DRIVER CAME FORWARD ANONYMOUSLY.
HE SAID THAT ON THAT NOVEMBER DAY, A MAN HAD JOINED THE WOMAN IN HIS CAB FOR THE RIDE TO THE RAILWAY STATION.
IN 2005, A BERGEN HIKER REPORTED A SIGHTING FROM FIVE DAYS BEFORE THE BODY WAS FOUND:
THE WOMAN, DRESSED FOR THE CITY, WALKING AHEAD OF TWO MEN IN COATS.
HE SAID HE WAS TOLD TO FORGET IT; NO FORMAL RECORD WAS MADE.
NONE OF THIS IS EVIDENCE OF MURDER. IT IS EVIDENCE OF PEOPLE WHO WERE NEVER FOUND —
AND OF A SCENE THAT ALWAYS ALLOWED MORE THAN ONE STORY.
THEN THERE IS THE THEORY EVERYONE HAS HEARD. THE COLD WAR CONTEXT:
A WOMAN WITH FALSE NAMES MOVING THROUGH A NATO COUNTRY.
THE CODES. THE DISCIPLINE. THE SILENCE.
JOURNALISTS NOTED THAT SOME OF HER MOVEMENTS COINCIDED WITH MISSILE TESTING AREAS ON NORWAY'S
COAST — AND A FISHERMAN PLACED HER NEAR ONE SUCH ZONE.
IT IS A SUGGESTIVE PATTERN, AND NOTHING MORE.
HERE IS WHAT THE FILE DOES NOT CONTAIN: NOT ONE DOCUMENT PLACING HER IN ANY INTELLIGENCE SERVICE.
NOT ONE WITNESS NAMING AN AGENCY. BERGEN POLICE NEVER ADOPTED THE SPY THEORY.
IT REMAINS EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS IN 1970 — A STORY THAT FITS THE SHAPE OF THE CLUES, BUT NONE
OF THE FACTS IN THE FILE PROVE IT. HOLD IT LIGHTLY.
IN 2016, BERGEN POLICE REOPENED THE CASE, AND THE MEDIA BROUGHT NEW ATTENTION.
NRK COMMISSIONED SIX NEW SKETCHES, SHOWN TO PEOPLE WHO HAD ACTUALLY SEEN HER.
THE BBC AND NORWAY'S NRK TURNED THE CASE INTO THE PODCAST DEATH IN ICE VALLEY, AND LISTENERS
AROUND THE WORLD BEGAN SENDING NEW LEADS.
THE REINVESTIGATION GATHERED WHAT THE 1970S COULD NOT:
FRESH INTERVIEWS, DIGITAL RESTORATIONS OF THE SKETCHES, AND THE FIRST FULL RE-EXAMINATION
OF THE PRESERVED EVIDENCE.
MODERN FORENSICS WENT TO WORK ON WHAT 1970 HAD PRESERVED.
ISOTOPE TESTING ON HER TEETH — KEPT SEPARATELY SINCE THE AUTOPSY —
PLACED HER BIRTH AROUND 1930, IN OR NEAR NUREMBERG, IN SOUTHERN GERMANY.
THE SAME ANALYSIS SUGGESTED SHE MOVED AS A CHILD TO FRANCE, OR THE FRENCH-GERMAN BORDER REGION
— WHICH MATCHED EARLIER HANDWRITING ANALYSIS POINTING TO A FRENCH EDUCATION.
HER DNA POINTED TO A MATERNAL LINE FOUND IN SOUTH-EASTERN EUROPE OR SOUTH-WESTERN ASIA.
GENETIC GENEALOGIST COLLEEN FITZPATRICK OF THE DNA DOE PROJECT JOINED THE EFFORT.
EVEN HER DENTIST SEEMED TO HAVE BEEN ABROAD: THE DENTAL WORK MATCHED PRACTICES IN CENTRAL
OR SOUTHERN EUROPE, EAST ASIA — OR SOUTH AMERICA.
EVERY ANSWER OPENED ANOTHER MAP.
SO STRIP AWAY FIFTY YEARS OF FOLKLORE. HERE IS WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS:
A WOMAN IN HER THIRTIES OR FORTIES, BORN AROUND 1930, TRAVELLING ALONE UNDER FALSE NAMES WITH GREAT CARE.
CONFIRMED: THE MEDICAL CAUSE OF DEATH, THE DATES, THE HOTELS, THE ALIASES, THE CODED NOTEBOOK,
THE 1971 VERDICT OF PROBABLE SUICIDE — AND THE 2016 REOPENING THAT CHANGED NONE OF IT.
DISPUTED: THE NECK INJURY. THE TWO-MEN SIGHTING.
THE TAXI PASSENGER. WHETHER ANY SECOND PERSON WAS EVER AT THE VALLEY FLOOR.
UNKNOWN: HER NAME. HER HOME COUNTRY — LIKELY SOUTHERN GERMANY OR THE FRENCH BORDER REGION,
BUT NEVER PROVEN. WHY SHE ERASED HER IDENTITY. AND WHETHER ANYONE HELPED HER DIE —
OR HELPED HER ERASE.
SHE LIES IN A ZINC COFFIN IN BERGEN, IN GROUND THAT HAS HELD HER FOR OVER FIFTY YEARS.
SOMEWHERE, THERE MAY BE A FAMILY ARCHIVE, A BIRTH RECORD, A NAME ON A PAGE —
THAT NO ONE HAS CHECKED.
THE ISDAL WOMAN. CASE 134, OF 1970. CASE STATUS: OPEN.
